summary:
Delaware is a state of the United States and stands under the national framework, which the national record and the parent bundle carry. What follows is Delaware's own law and practice.

A national trans legal risk assessment dated July 2026 places Delaware in its Low-Risk States group, alongside Arizona, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Wisconsin and the District of Columbia, defined as jurisdictions that largely refrain from targeting transgender adults without specialising in their protection.

Delaware has no state ban on transgender people using public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity, per the Movement Advancement Project equality map, which tracks such bans state by state.

Since 2013 Delaware law prohibits discrimination on the basis of actual or perceived gender identity in employment, housing, public accommodations and other areas. The statute, SB 97, passed the Senate 11-7 on 6 June 2013, passed the House 24-17 with amendments, cleared the Senate on amendments 11-9 on 18 June, was signed the following day and took effect immediately.

Since 2013 Delaware has imposed additional penalties for a violent crime motivated by the victim's actual or perceived gender identity.

HB142, which would formally repeal the common-law gay and trans panic defence and ban its use, was introduced in May 2023 and passed both houses of the Legislature in June 2023; the Governor has neither signed nor vetoed it, so its final status is unresolved in this record.

Transgender people may change their legal gender on state-issued identification on the signed statement of a licensed medical provider alone. Since 11 February 2017 sex reassignment surgery has not been an explicit requirement for an amended birth certificate; the requirement is instead a signed affidavit of surgical, hormonal, psychological or other treatment appropriate for gender transition. As of April 2020 Delaware did not offer a gender X marker on drivers licences, and no later source in this record updates that position.

A law signed 25 June 2015 and effective immediately allows inmates to access and change the name on birth certificates to reflect gender identity, where previously inmates could change names only for religious reasons.

Since 26 March 2016 Delaware has prohibited discrimination based on gender identity within insurance contracts, including coverage of sex reassignment surgery.

Delaware SB 65, introduced 26 April 2017 and signed and effective 23 July 2018 as Laws of Delaware 81:340, defines conversion therapy to include practices seeking to change gender identity, behaviour or gender expression. It makes the practice unprofessional conduct subject to discipline for physicians, nurses, mental health and chemical dependency professionals, psychologists and clinical social workers performed on a minor, bars referring a minor out of state for it, and prohibits the Department of Services for Children, Youth and Their Families from performing or recommending it for a minor.

Executive Order Eight of 11 August 2009 extended anti-discrimination safeguards to state employees and applicants on the basis of gender identity and reauthorised the Governor's Council on Equal Employment Opportunity with a charge to foster an inclusive environment among executive-branch employees. In January 2025 Governor Hall-Long signed an executive order creating Delaware's LGBTQ+ Commission.

Civil unions carrying the rights, benefits, protections and responsibilities of married persons became available on 1 January 2012, and same-sex marriage was legalised effective 1 July 2013 with conversion of existing civil unions to marriages.
tangentialFactors:
The July 2026 assessment's Low-Risk grouping is a comparative ranking by state policy posture rather than a measure of incident rates; it groups Delaware with seven other states and the District of Columbia on the criterion of not targeting transgender adults, and the source provides no per-capita or enforcement data behind the placement.

Delaware's protections sit within a national environment the parent record documents as deteriorating: the same assessment names four states as do-not-travel for trans people and records the 2026 legislative season as continuing to degrade trans rights. Delaware is placed on the opposite side of that classification.

Two Delaware bills affecting sexual-orientation protections remain unfinished in this record: a May 2021 measure to close a single-orientation loophole, which the Governor has not signed or vetoed, and HB275, which passed the House 21-15 on 28 March 2024 to include asexual and pansexual people in the definition of sexual orientation and awaits a Senate vote.

Federal custody policy on housing transgender prisoners has shifted repeatedly: a January 2015 ICE memo directed housing by gender identity, 2016 Department of Justice guidelines forbade assigning inmates to units solely on birth anatomy, and a 2018 Federal Bureau of Prisons revision made biological sex the initial determination with gender identity used only in rare cases. No Delaware-specific placement policy is documented in this record.
localsOnly:
State executive-branch employees and applicants have been covered against gender-identity discrimination by executive order since 11 August 2009, independently of the 2013 statute, and the Governor's Council on Equal Employment Opportunity carries an inclusion mandate for those workplaces.

Residents seeking a gender-marker change on state identification need only a signed statement from a licensed medical provider, and since 11 February 2017 an amended birth certificate requires an affidavit of transition treatment rather than proof of surgery.

Since 25 June 2015 incarcerated Delawareans have been able to access or change the name on a birth certificate to reflect gender identity, a right previously limited to name changes for religious belief.

Insurance contracts issued in Delaware have covered gender-identity-based discrimination, including sex reassignment surgery, since 26 March 2016.

Conversion therapy aimed at a minor's gender identity has been prohibited and professionally sanctionable since 23 July 2018, including where a minor is referred out of state for it, and the state child-services department may neither perform nor recommend it.

Violent crime motivated by a victim's actual or perceived gender identity carries additional penalties under Delaware law, a provision in force since 2013.

Delaware's LGBTQ+ Commission has existed since the executive order of January 2025.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Movement Advancement Project equality map page recording Delaware's absence of a public-facilities ban was not retrievable at the archived URL (HTTP 404); the finding rests on the map's underlying state-by-state tracking as cited, and the page itself could not be re-checked.

HB142's status is unresolved in this record: it passed both legislative chambers in June 2023 but no signing or veto is documented, so whether the gay and trans panic defence has been statutorily repealed is not established here.

No source in this inventory reports a Delaware-specific rule on the gender marker X for state identification after April 2020, so the current availability of an X marker on Delaware driving credentials is not sourced.

No Delaware-specific policy on the placement of transgender inmates in state custody is documented; the placement material in this inventory concerns federal agencies only and belongs to the national record.

This inventory contains no Delaware-specific data on entry screening, document seizure, arrest, or violence against transgender people, and no Delaware incident with a date is recorded; the risk picture rests on statutory protections and a single July 2026 classification.
